newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish share index and volume hit new records.
newsitem.headline: Turkish share index and volume hit new records.

text.p: Istanbul shares surged to the year's 17th record close on Monday as the market's strong uptrend persisted amid high turnover, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at an all-time high of 1,700, up 197 points, or 13.11 percent from Friday's previous record of 1,503. In dollar terms, it stood at a new record of 1.47 cents, compared to Friday's 1.3 cents.
Daily volume also soared to a record of 69.48 trillion lira ($602.3 million) from 64.87 trillion ($564.1 million) on Friday.
Brokers said profit-taking caused the index to retreat from a high of 1,727 it brushed at the start of the second session.

"There was brief profit-taking in the afternoon, again followed by buying. The market currently has no alternative, so the uptrend persists despite worries that the rise is too fast," said Tunc Salman from Korfez investment.

The index's non-stop gains have totalled 74.2 percent so far this year. In dollar terms, it jumped 61.5 percent since end-1996. Last year, the index had risen 143.8 percent and 35.8 percent in dollar terms.

Falling money and bond market rates, a quiet currency market, firms' 1996 profit prospects, lower-than-expected December inflation and 1996 budget deficit as well as progress in privatisation have boosted demand for shares since end-1996.
Brokers said foreign investor interest was another leading source of the recent liquidity influx to the market.

The uptrend was further buoyed by positive sentiment caused by last Thursday's contitutional court ruling giving green light to Turk Telekom's sell-off. The index has gone up 449 points, or 36 percent since last Wednesday's 1,251 close.
